title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
statement: Return the k-th smallest value (1-indexed) in a valid BST.

hints.1_question: In-order traversal of a BST visits values in increasing order. How can you stop as soon as you have visited k of them?
hints.2_nudge: Do an iterative in-order traversal with a stack and a counter.
hints.3_big_hint: Walk left pushing nodes; pop, decrement k; when k hits 0 return that node's value; otherwise go right.

known_bugs.name: returns the k-th largest
known_bugs.followup: In-order from the left gives increasing values. Which side are you walking first?

known_bugs.name: pre-order instead of in-order
known_bugs.followup: Does pre-order visit values in sorted order?

known_bugs.name: off-by-one index into the in-order list
known_bugs.followup: k is 1-indexed. Which index of the sorted list holds the k-th smallest?

followups: How would you handle frequent inserts/deletes and many kth queries (augment nodes with subtree sizes)?
Why is an iterative in-order better than building the whole list?
